<!-- page 589 -->
All Permanent Officials to Contribute to Retirement Fund

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, September 30, 1923.

SIR, - My attention has been drawn to the fact that none of the employees in the outside service of your department
contribute to the Retirement Fund, with the exception, perhaps, of one or two who were transferred from the inside
service.

I beg to point out that as the present Civil Service Act applies to the officers in the outside service of your department,
the Civil Service Superannuation and Retirement Act also applies to those officers, and in consequence an abatement
of five per cent should be made each month from the salaries of all your permanent employees and remitted to the
Finance Department for deposit in the Retirement Fund.

Kindly see that this abatement for the Retirement Fund is made in all future payments of salary.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Travelling Expenses of Ottawa Officials should be paid from Civil Government Contingencies

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, October 11, 1923.

SIR, - I have before me two accounts, amounting to $780.62, for the expenses of Mr. D.F. Robertson, chief surveyor of
your department, when visiting Brantford between January 24th and March 20th last. I understand from your
accounting branch that Mr. Robertson was acting as agent at the Six Nations Reserve during that period. In these
accounts I find several items to which I have to take exception.

No vouchers or receipts are given in support of the following payments:

Jan. 27th, Kerby House, board and lodging $11 50
Feb 9th, Kerby House, board and lodging 61 78

Receipted vouchers showing in detail how these amounts are arrived at should be furnished by Mr. Robertson.

On four occasions during the period covered by Mr. Robertson's accounts he appears to have returned to Ottawa for the
week end, arriving in Ottawa on Saturday morning and leaving again on Sunday night, at a cost of approximately $30
for each trip. I should like to be assured that each of these week end trips was necessarily undertaken on departmental
business.

In connection with these week end trips I notice that Mr. Robertson makes the following charges for meals at Ottawa:

January 28 $3 75
January 29 3 75
February 10 2 75
February 11 3 75
February 25 3 75
February 26 3 75
March 21 1 25
...         $22 75
